messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: capacity_surge detected in us-west-2-prod
- signal: tokens_per_sec > 95th percentile
- throttle_rate: 7.8% sustained over 3m
- queue_depth: short-term growth 2.7x baseline

Maya R: seeing the alert. I'm seeing elevated 429s at the L7 gateway, no customer pages yet.

Kia (oncall): grabbing the page. @Maya R can you scope impact by route and model?

Maya R: mostly /v1/generate and a couple of small-chat routes. p50 latency +40ms, p99 up ~600ms. error ratio jumped 0.2% -> 2.1% on those routes.

Jon P: perf team joined. Can someone pull tokens/sec by model and pool? I want per-shard breakdown.

Alex T: tailing the logs now, quick grep shows a single model variant spiking:
```
2026-03-14T15:12:01Z model=redwood-llama shards=3 tokens/sec=183000 throttles=120
2026-03-14T15:13:01Z model=redwood-llama shards=3 tokens/sec=192000 throttles=160
```
Looks concentrated on that model pool.

Samira: customer-impact note: tracing shows ~5% of requests in the 15:12-15:19 window got 429s. No formal support escalations yet.

Kia (oncall): mitigation options quick list: 1) enable model fallback to smaller variant for interactive routes, 2) raise autoscaler soft cap, 3) suppress noisy pages while we mitigate. Pros/cons?

Maya R: 1) is the least risky for user experience. 2) scale-up will take minutes; may not stop immediate throttles. 3) agreed: suppress token spike pages selectively to avoid paging loops while we act.

Jon P: proposed immediate plan:
- suppress tokens_per_sec pager for 20m (keep dashboard alerts)
- route non-critical /batch and short-chat to redwood-llama-small
- add per-shard queue_depth tile to default SRE dashboard for visibility

Kia (oncall): running suppression:
```
opsctl alert suppress --id capacity_surge --scope us-west-2-prod --for 20m --reason "active mitigations: fallback + shard inspection"
```
:white_check_mark: suppression applied (20m)

Alex T: pushing a small routing change to route-chat rules:
```
if route in ["/chat/short"] and tokens/sec > 120000 -> model=redwood-llama-small
```
Canarying in us-west-2 now.

Samira: putting a brief customer blurb in CSM channel with mitigation timeline. No customers asking for credits at the moment.

Jon P: also bumped autoscaler soft cap for the affected pool +25% as a temporary buffer:
```
autoscale update --pool inference-usw2-llama --soft-cap-multiplier 1.25
```
Will revert after we stabilize.

Maya R: canary shows cutover to small model reduced throttles on interactive routes. p99 back toward baseline for short-chat. Heavy long-generations still showing backlog.

incident-bot: metric update: tokens_per_sec down to ~82% baseline after routing change; throttle_rate down to 1.0%.

Kia (oncall): post-incident followups to add to ticket and runbook:
- change tokens_per_sec pager to multi-signal: require (tokens_per_sec > X) AND (throttle_rate > Y) OR (queue_depth > Z)
- add per-shard queue_depth + tokens_per_shard tiles to default SRE dashboard
- implement automated fallback policy for redwood-llama when sustained tokens/sec > threshold for 2m
- review autoscaler cooldown and responsiveness (consider shorter cooldown or staged scaling)

Jon P: sketched alert prototype (Prom-like for our alert engine):
```
alert: CapacityAnomaly
expr: (
  (sum(rate(tokens_total[1m])) by (pool) > 150000)
  and (sum(rate(throttles_total[1m])) by (pool) > 0.01)
)
for: 3m
```
Pager only when both load and throttles are present.

Maya R: also recommend adjusting queue_depth thresholds per-pool. current static threshold = 100 is too noisy for busy pools; suggest 250 for busiest and add exponential decay to avoid transient spikes.

Kia (oncall): opening follow-up ticket -> https://tickets.internal/REDWOOD-4321
Summary: "Multi-signal capacity alert + dashboard + autoscale cooldown review"
Assignees: eng-sre, perf, infra. ETA: alert PR by EOW, autoscale tuning next week.

Alex T: leaving a note to attach replay dataset for 15:00-15:30 window for perf evals.

Samira: posted a short incident note to CSM slack with timeline & mitigations. Will escalate if customers reply.

Maya R: monitoring until suppression expires. If throttles reappear we un-suppress and escalate.

Kia (oncall): thanks all. Scheduling a 30min sync tomorrow to finalize alert logic and runbook diffs.

Jon P: reaction :eyes:
Maya R: reaction :heart:
incident-bot: STATUS: mitigated -> monitoring"
